## Summary

Test-first contract for the follow-source interface and unlock/persistence logic using a mocked Steamworks session, written before the implementation features (F3/F4). Defines the interface the renderer and unlock logic consume so the Steam SDK stays behind an abstraction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A mockable `FollowSource` interface is defined (init, isSteamAvailable, openStorePage, isFollowing, claim) with a deterministic fake implementation.
- [ ] Unit tests (`tests/steam-follow/`) cover: follow detected → unlock flow triggered; already-unlocked → no re-verification prompt; Steam absent → graceful degraded path (no crash); choose-one-of-three catalog resolution; unlock persistence round-trip across simulated launches.
- [ ] Tests run and pass under `--project unit` (fast, no browser).
- [ ] The interface contract documents that the renderer never imports the Steam SDK directly.

## Minimal Implementation

- Test-only feature: interface + test doubles + unit tests.
- Reference the launcher item's content-locator abstraction (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) for the dependency-injection pattern.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (launcher) for the abstraction pattern it establishes.

## Deliverables

- `FollowSource` interface + mocked unit tests.

# Task: Verify fresh remote clones — game repos and launcher presets

## Goal

As a game developer, a fresh clone of a published game repo (with the engine
pulled in through the `core` submodule) installs, builds and unit-tests
successfully; and as a distribution builder the launcher can compose a subset of
the remote repos as siblings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In a clean temporary directory,
   `git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tce-golf.git`
   followed by `npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit`
   succeeds.
2. The same sequence succeeds for `tce-main-street` (parent AC3).
3. A fresh clone of `tableau-card-engine-core` succeeds and
   `npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit` passes inside
   it.
4. The launcher composes a subset of the **remote** repos as siblings against
   fresh clones: `GAMES_CONFIG=solo` and `GAMES_CONFIG=full` builds
   (`npm run build`) both succeed (parent AC4).
5. The exact commands executed and their outcomes are recorded on the parent
   work item as verification evidence; any failure is triaged into a critical
   `test-failure` work item rather than worked around.

## Minimal Implementation

- Clone into a clean temp directory (never reuse a prior checkout) so the
  submodule resolution on clone is genuinely exercised.
- Run the clone/build/test sequence for golf and main-street, plus core.
- For the launcher presets, clone the remote game repos as siblings under the
  paths the presets reference (`../tce-<game>`) and build with `GAMES_CONFIG`
  set to `solo` then `full`.
- Record failures with the exact command and output before triaging.

**Key Files:**

- `configs/solo.json` — the one-game preset spot check.
- `configs/full.json` — the all-games preset spot check.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — sibling-repo discovery used by the
  presets.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — the documented clone/build/test workflow under test.

**Dependencies:**

**C4** (the repositories must exist and be pushed before a fresh clone can be
verified).

**Deliverables:**

- Fresh-clone verification evidence for golf, main-street, core and the
  `solo`/`full` launcher presets, recorded on the parent.
data.title: Verify fresh remote clones: game repos and launcher presets

# Task: Publish the documented state, record evidence and pass the full-suite gate

## Goal

As a maintainer the documentation describes the published multi-repo reality
(not the "remotes are not created" state), the parent's publication evidence is
recorded, and the acceptance-test gates (script suites plus the full project
suite) pass at the final commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 ("GitHub remotes are not created in
   this phase") is replaced with the published state: the nine repo names, public
   visibility, `dev`/`main` (default `main`), the `core` submodule path, and the
   idempotent re-run semantics; §6 (follow-on work) reflects only what genuinely
   remains.
2. `README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` document the clone-with-submodules
   workflow for a single game repo: `git clone --recurse-submodules <repo>`,
   `npm install`, `npm run build`, `npm test -- --project unit`.
3. No documentation still claims the `tce-*` remotes do not exist, and the
   published commands in the docs match those verified by C5 (parent AC7,
   including code comments where behaviour changed).
4. The per-repo retained commit counts and the source `dev` SHA are recorded on
   the parent CG-0MUHK5NND0024J1S (parent AC5).
5. `npx vitest run --project unit tests/scripts/` passes, including the
   extraction, scaffold and publication suites (parent AC8).
6. The full project test suite (`npm test`) passes at the final commit
   (parent AC9).

## Minimal Implementation

- Update the architecture doc's "remotes not created" narrative and the
  follow-on inventory first, since those are the statements that are now false.
- Add the clone-with-submodules quick start to `README.md` and
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, reusing the exact commands verified in C5.
- Record the consolidated evidence table (repo → retained commit count, source
  `dev` SHA) as a parent comment.
- Run the script unit suites and then the full suite from a clean checkout at
  the final commit; triage any failure per the test-failure policy.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — published-state narrative and
  follow-on inventory.
- `./README.md` — clone-with-submodules quick start.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — single-game repo build/test workflow.
- `./AGENTS.md` — project guidance if the workflow statement there needs
  aligning.

**Dependencies:**

**C5** (the docs must describe a verified state, not an assumed one).

**Deliverables:**

- Updated user/developer documentation for the published repositories.
- Parent evidence comment (commit counts plus source SHA).
- Green script unit suites and a green full project suite at the final commit.
data.title: Publish documented state, record evidence and pass the full-suite gate

## Goal

Fix the shared `HandView` so that, when `maxSlots` is set, card and outline positions derive from the hand's **capacity** rather than the current card count — adding a card never moves an existing card or slot.

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Sibling test items add the failing unit and browser tests first.

Root cause: `computeCardPositions()` builds a row centred on `this.cards.length` (`layoutCardPositions({ count: this.cards.length, … })`), and `_computeOutlineSlots()` ghosts it (plus appending extras). The empty-hand branch already lays out the desired fixed `maxSlots` row, so that row is the template to reuse. `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path all re-derive the row/rotation normalisation from the occupied positions and must move to the template as well. `setMaxSlots()` currently only rebuilds outlines and does not re-lay the cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1–AC5: implement the capacity-template behaviour — outline slot positions identical for a hand of 0…`maxSlots` cards; `addCard` fills the next slot right of the occupied run while pre-existing card positions are unchanged; occupied outlines still match card `x/y/rotation` with extras below every card; `setMaxSlots(n)` is the only mutation that re-lays the row and always yields exactly `n` slots; the empty-hand capacity row is unchanged (same centred straight/arc row the cards will occupy).
- Add a shared private helper in `src/ui/HandView.ts` that derives the `maxSlots` template with the existing `layoutCardPositions` maths (gap = `spacing - cardWidth`, `centerX`, `maxWidth` compression, `arcRadius` Y) and the template-span rotation normalisation; recompute from current options on each use (no stale cache).
- `computeCardPositions()` horizontal returns the first `cards.length` template positions; over-capacity cards continue with the template step to the right (best-effort, no re-centring).
- `getInsertionPosition(index)` returns the template position at `index` (first `maxSlots`; template step beyond), so Market→hand transfer animations land exactly on the resting card.
- `_computeOutlineSlots()` derives all `count` slots from the same template (occupied slots ghost the card's **actual** sprite rotation, extras keep `depth = index - 0.5 - count`), replacing the per-count ghosting/extension branch.
- Rotation and arc normalisation in `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path use the template span when `maxSlots` is set, so per-card rotation is also stable across adds.
- `setMaxSlots(maxSlots)` re-lays the cards (calls `applyLayout()`), not just the outlines.
- Capacity-driven layout is keyed on `maxSlots !== undefined`, independent of `showPositionOutlines`; toggling outlines never moves cards.
- Hands without `maxSlots` keep the existing centred-on-count layout; vertical cascade keeps `baseY + i * spacing` and is not regressed.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` is reused unchanged.
- The sibling unit and browser test items pass (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `computeCardPositions()`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`, `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, `sortCards()` animated path, `setMaxSlots()`.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — reused to build the capacity row (no change expected).

**Deliverables:**

- Capacity-driven `HandView` layout with stable card and outline slots and green sibling tests.
data.title: Capacity-driven HandView slot template

## Goal

Document the capacity-driven (stable) slot semantics and remove stale wording that describes the hand as centred on the **current** card count (parent AC8).

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. The fix changes documented behaviour, so the doc-update policy applies: the change and its docs must ship together (or this child blocks parent closure).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC8: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Hand capacity outlines), `AGENTS.md` if the documented behaviour changes, and any relevant Gym/docs entries.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` "Hand capacity outlines" states that when `maxSlots` is set the slot row is derived from **capacity**, cards fill it left-to-right, occupied card/slot positions do not move as cards are added, and `setMaxSlots()` is the only operation that re-lays the row; the empty-hand row is unchanged.
- `AGENTS.md` §2 (HandView/PileView key features) hand bullet updated to say slots/outlines are capacity-derived and stable across adds.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` help text describes the fixed-slot behaviour instead of implying per-count centring.
- Stale per-count-centring comments corrected in at least: `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` ("centred on handCenterX" / "left-anchored slot estimate"), `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` ("centred on handCenterX"), and `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` (hand-zone comment).
- No player- or developer-facing text still claims the hand is centred on the current card count when `maxSlots` is set.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — "Hand capacity outlines" section.
- `./AGENTS.md` — §2 hand bullet (and §9 if it repeats the layout claim).
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — help text.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — stale comments.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — stale comment.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` — hand-zone comment.

**Deliverables:**

- Updated docs and stale comments matching the shipped behaviour.

## Goal

Verify the complete change set end-to-end and make the parent audit-ready (parent AC9).

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Final verification item; depends on the implementation and docs siblings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC9: full project test suite must pass with the new changes — `/skill:test` (quiet mode, triaged) green at the commit under review, which populates the per-repo audit test cache.
- `npm run build` succeeds (TypeScript compile + Vite bundle).
- Unit profile (`npm test -- --project unit`) green.
- Smoke and dev profiles (`npm run test:smoke`, `npm run test:dev`) green.
- Main Street browser suite (including the market→hand click/drag/transfer paths that read `getInsertionPosition`) green, confirming the `handCenterX` anchoring/transfer risk did not materialise.
- Any regression is fixed in-scope or triaged into a linked `test-failure` work item; all tests must pass before `in_review`.
- Commit hash(es) recorded in a comment on this item and the parent.
- Parent AC1–AC9 verified met and `/skill:audit` reports ready for review.

**Deliverables:**

- Green build + unit/smoke/dev/browser/full runs and a recorded verification comment.
